clue.text: Starts displays

definitions.meaning: to start a journey or a process is to begin it, as when a runner leaves the blocks
a frame or a colour that shows something to advantage is said to enhance it in this sense

explanation.surface: A terse note that something begins its shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: one means begins or triggers, the other means enhances by contrast, as a scarf does an outfit.

clue.text: Quickly buys drink after crack is made

indicators.note: after places the word for drink behind the word for crack

parts.note: a crack is a sharp breaking sound, a snap
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a bargain and celebrates with a drink once a breakthrough comes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to purchase eagerly before anyone else can, as shoppers do at a sale.

clue.text: Say everything it turned up is harrowing among other things

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the whole run of pieces is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG
everything means all

explanation.surface: It sounds like someone describing a whole ordeal that came to light as distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses EG + ALL + IT, giving the letters backwards. 'Harrowing' looks like an adjective for distress, but here it is the farming job of breaking up soil with a harrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Cultivation of land includes ploughing and harrowing, so harrowing is one example of the work.

clue.text: Fancy both the round and long

parts.note: a round thing is shaped like the letter O
to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: Someone likes both the circular and the lengthy option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' is a verb here, meaning to suppose or think, and 'long' is a verb too, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy that something is so is to believe or state it as a view.

clue.text: Member of an association for seamen possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the phrase for seamen might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor's club might have a sailor as a member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' asks for an anagram of FOR SEAMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mason belongs to a fraternal society with lodges, a well-known secretive association.

clue.text: Score, not being handicapped

definitions.meaning: to score a surface is to mark it with a sharp point
a golfer playing off zero handicap is said to be at this level

explanation.surface: A sports report notes a result achieved without any handicap.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to mark with a claw or point, and in golf describes a player who receives no strokes of handicap.

clue.text: Determined to raise money

indicators.note: in a down clue raise means the word is lifted so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: banknotes are money

explanation.surface: A person resolved to go fundraising.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bent on something is to be resolved to do it.

clue.text: Jogger grabbing a rest

indicators.note: grabbing means the prompt word holds the A inside it

parts.note: a memory jogger is a prompt or memo

explanation.surface: A runner snatches a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogger' suggests a runner, but it is something that jogs the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest is what is left over, the balance.

clue.text: The setting of this lever might be altered

indicators.note: setting refers to a new arrangement of the letters of altered, the clue's last word

explanation.surface: A remark that the adjustment of a lever could be changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot-operated bar that drives a wheel, as on an old sewing machine, is a kind of lever.

clue.text: Weight-lifters a fellow maintains

parts.note: a fellow is referred to as he
to maintain a claim is to aver it

explanation.surface: A man claims something about weightlifting athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who lift heavy things with effort are lifters of weight.

clue.text: A fifties item adapted to be up to date?

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties give LL

indicators.note: adapted means the letters of item are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of 1950s memorabilia is modernised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifties' looks like a decade but is two Roman fifties. 'adapted' makes TIME from ITEM.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time record covers every result up to the present, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Annoyance with a manufacturer of emulsion paint

parts.note: annoyance or anger is temper

explanation.surface: Someone is cross with a paint company.
explanation.definitionFit: This artists' medium is pigment bound in an emulsion, traditionally of egg yolk.

clue.text: Americans in the Senate?

parts.note: read the Americans as men from the States; senators are also distinguished politicians

explanation.definitionFit: Senior political figures are senators, and US senators are literally men of the States.

clue.text: Not out just to furnish

parts.note: a batsman not out is still in
just means deserved or due

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire's call that seems fair.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who is NOT OUT is still IN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variant of endue, meaning to provide or invest with a quality.

clue.text: The City's into convenience food and scrap

indicators.note: into means the City's code goes inside the food

parts.note: a ready-made pie is a convenience food
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: London's financial district takes on ready meals and junk.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a fragment or bit.

clue.text: Continuance without stress

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or without, as in ex dividend
stress means strain or tension

explanation.surface: A carry-on that comes free of strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolongation of time, as for a deadline, is a continuance.

clue.text: Pronounce on the head's good judgement

parts.note: to pronounce a letter is to sound it
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: Someone speaks about the headteacher's wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: A head is a headland; NESS is the old word for one, common in British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliability of reasoning or sound sense is good judgement.

clue.text: Franco-British articles board can't be taken in!

parts.note: une is the French indefinite article
a is the English indefinite article
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A complaint that French and British reports on a board's affairs are hard to believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't be taken in' looks like disbelief but means not fit to swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Food unfit to eat cannot be swallowed.

clue.text: Buses can't accommodate the stuff

indicators.note: accommodate means the letters are fitted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Public transport hasn't room for the luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter or material is stuff.

clue.text: Non-commissioned men in torment dealing with mail

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the pain word

parts.note: a sting is sharp pain or torment
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not commissioned officers

explanation.surface: Ordinary soldiers suffer while handling the post.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the army term for non-commissioned soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Post offices separate letters by destination as part of handling post.

clue.text: Investment over time means loss of freedom

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the investment sits above the time word

parts.note: a bond is a fixed-interest investment
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Tying up money long-term means sacrificing liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavery or captivity is the state of lacking liberty.

clue.text: Comment added on a horse

definitions.meaning: an addendum or extra clause attached to a statement
a person mounted and travelling on horseback

explanation.surface: A remark tacked on about horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a clause appended to a document and a person on horseback.

clue.text: She'll provide a player with change

definitions.text: She'll provide a player with change

parts.words: She'll provide a player with change
parts.note: read player as an actor and change as a costume change in the wings, not as coins

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre wardrobe assistant helps performers into their costumes.

clue.text: The eccentric is rude to the egghead 6

indicators.note: eccentric means the letters of is rude behave oddly and are rearranged

parts.note: the head of the word egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: An odd person is rude to an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges IS RUDE to RESIDU; 'egghead' is the head of egg. 6 points to the answer to 6 Down, REMAINDER.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over after removal is the rest, a synonym of the cross-referenced answer.

clue.text: Drive new cars and wreck about a quarter

indicators.note: about means the wreck word goes round the compass letter

parts.note: to wreck is to ruin
N, north, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Joyriders take fresh vehicles and smash them around a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' is a compass point, here N.
explanation.definitionFit: New engines were once driven gently at first to bed in their parts.

clue.text: Superior, but unsuited?

definitions.meaning: read as lacking a match, having nothing to pair with

explanation.surface: Is it better, or just a bad fit?
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means without an equal; the playful second reading is without anything to pair with.

clue.text: Young person having a thousand in gold

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
taken as written
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A youngster with a fortune in gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under the age of legal adulthood is a juvenile.

clue.text: Save nothing in difficult situation

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the word for difficult

parts.note: difficult means hard
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Advice to put nothing aside when times are tough.
explanation.definitionFit: To store up or stockpile is to save.

clue.text: A European would give it a secure backing

indicators.note: backing means the word for secure is turned to read backwards

parts.note: to secure with fastenings is to nail

explanation.surface: A continental would support it securely.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Italy is a European.

clue.text: A variety of bread is cooked

indicators.note: a variety of means the letters of bread and is are made into a different form

explanation.surface: One type of loaf has been baked.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow-cooked in a little liquid in a covered pot, a method of cooking.

clue.text: The less sophisticated the more colourful!

definitions.meaning: more naive or inexperienced, as a raw beginner
of a deeper leafy colour, playfully called more colourful

explanation.surface: The more naive someone is, the more vivid they seem.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative means both more naive, like a novice, and more verdant in colour.

clue.text: Finish by trimming rose back

parts.note: finish means end

indicators.note: trimming means the letters of rose are adjusted into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener completes the job by pruning a rose bush at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a direction, but it is a verb meaning to support. 'trimming' rearranges ROSE to ORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To support a candidate or sign the reverse of a cheque is to back it.
